```{r libraries}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)

# Unified color palette: technology colors (ONT = Blue, PacBio = Orange) matching
# all other figures, plus a single shared grey for all spike-in groups.
color_palette <- c(
  "ONT dRNA"  = "#56B4E9",  # Soft Blue
  "ONT cDNA"  = "#D1B490",  # Sandy gold
  "Iso-Seq"   = "#EE7B30",  # Orange
  "Kinnex"    = "#e31c93",  # PacBio pink
  "Short SIRV" = "#969696", # Grey (shared with all spike-ins)
  "Long SIRV"  = "#969696", # Grey (shared with all spike-ins)
  "ERCC"       = "#969696"  # Grey (shared with all spike-ins)
)
```

```{r theme_and_colors}
# Strict Nature-style theme, matching Fig 1 Panel B
theme_nature <- function(base_size = 6.5, base_family = "sans") {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) +
    theme(
      axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.35, colour = "black"),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.35, colour = "black"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = base_size),
      axis.text = element_text(size = base_size - 0.5, color = "black"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = base_size - 0.3),
      legend.text = element_text(size = base_size - 0.7),
      strip.text = element_text(size = base_size - 0.3, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_size + 0.5, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}

theme_set(theme_nature())
```

```{r load_read_lengths}
# Sampled read-length files produced by helper_scripts/sample_read_lengths_array.sh
#   One gzip-compressed file per (dataset, technology):
#     <dir>/<Dataset>_<Technology>_read_lengths.txt.gz
#   with one read length (bp) per line.
read_lengths_dir <- "data/lengths"
length_files <- list.files(read_lengths_dir, pattern = "_read_lengths\\.txt\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE)

read_lengths <- length_files |>
  setNames(basename(length_files)) |>
  lapply(function(f) {
    file_base <- sub("_read_lengths\\.txt\\.gz$", "", basename(f))
    # <Dataset>_<Technology> -> split on the FIRST underscore
    tech_idx <- regexpr("_", file_base, fixed = TRUE)
    dataset <- substr(file_base, 1, tech_idx - 1)
    technology <- substr(file_base, tech_idx + 1, nchar(file_base))
    tibble(
      length_bp = as.numeric(read_lines(f)),
      dataset = dataset,
      technology = technology
    )
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

# Normalize technology naming to the shared palette keys.
# Handles the inconsistent casing observed in the files (e.g. ONT_CDNA vs ONT_cDNA).
technology_map <- c(
  "ONT_dRNA" = "ONT dRNA",
  "ONT_drna" = "ONT dRNA",
  "ONT_CDNA" = "ONT cDNA",
  "ONT_cDNA" = "ONT cDNA",
  "ONT_cdna" = "ONT cDNA",
  "IsoSeq"    = "Iso-Seq",
  "isoseq"    = "Iso-Seq",
  "Kinnex"    = "Kinnex",
  "kinnex"    = "Kinnex"
)
read_lengths$technology <- unname(technology_map[read_lengths$technology])

# Standardize dataset names for consistent ordering
read_lengths$dataset[read_lengths$dataset == "NIH"] <- "Mouse"
read_lengths$dataset[read_lengths$dataset == "Neuron"] <- "iNeuron"

read_lengths$category <- "Reads"
```

```{r load_spikein_lengths}
# Spike-in lengths files, one length (bp) per line (no header), global across
# the datasets/technologies.
spikein_lengths <- bind_rows(
  tibble(length_bp = as.numeric(read_lines("data/lengths/ERCCS_lengths.txt")), category = "ERCC"),
  tibble(length_bp = as.numeric(read_lines("data/lengths/SIRVS_lengths.txt")), category = "SIRV")
)
```

```{r combine}
# Reads panel data: facet = "Reads", x = dataset, technology = actual technology
read_lengths$facet <- "Reads"

# Spike-in panel data: facet = "Spike-ins", x = dataset = "spike-ins" (all),
# SIRVs split into long (>= 4 kb) and short (< 4 kb). The spike-in type is stored
# in `technology` so the same workflow colors both panels.
spikein_lengths <- spikein_lengths %>%
  mutate(
    technology = case_when(
      category == "SIRV" & length_bp >= 4000 ~ "Long SIRV",
      category == "SIRV" & length_bp < 4000  ~ "Short SIRV",
      category == "ERCC"                     ~ "ERCC",
      TRUE                                   ~ category
    ),
    facet = "Spike-ins",
    dataset = "spike-ins"
  )

all_lengths <- bind_rows(read_lengths, spikein_lengths)

# Explicit, unique group id per (facet, dataset, technology) so dodge works even
# when the boxplot fill is a constant ("white") - this keeps all spike groups
# and technologies separate.
all_lengths$grp <- as.integer(factor(interaction(all_lengths$facet, all_lengths$dataset, all_lengths$technology)))

# Factor levels for clean ordering
all_lengths$facet <- factor(all_lengths$facet, levels = c("Reads", "Spike-ins"))
all_lengths$dataset <- factor(all_lengths$dataset, levels = c("Mouse", "iNeuron", "LongBench", "spike-ins"))
all_lengths$technology <- factor(all_lengths$technology,
                                levels = c("ONT dRNA", "ONT cDNA", "Iso-Seq", "Kinnex",
                                           "Short SIRV", "Long SIRV", "ERCC"))
```

```{r generate_plots}
# Boxplot + violin (no points), faceted between Reads and Spike-ins.
# Reads:     x = dataset, dodged by technology, colored by technology.
# Spike-ins: x = "spike-ins", dodged by spike group (Short/Long SIRV, ERCC).
p <- ggplot(all_lengths, aes(x = technology, y = length_bp)) +
  # 1. Desaturated soft violin plot for the distribution (fill = technology)
  geom_violin(
    aes(group = grp, fill = technology),
    width = 0.6,
    alpha = 0.6,
    color = NA,
    scale = "width",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  # 2. Narrow boxplot (white fill, dark outline) - dodge grouped by the explicit
  #    grp so all groups stay separate; the fill color comes from the violin
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(group = grp),
    width = 0.12,
    color = "#272727",
    fill = "white",
    alpha = 0.9,
    linewidth = 0.3,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Length (bp)") +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

```{r export}
# Professional high-impact export function
save_pub_r <- function(plot, filename, width_mm = 180, height_mm = 120, dpi = 600) {
  w <- width_mm / 25.4
  h <- height_mm / 25.4

  # Lossless Vector SVG
  svglite::svglite(paste0(filename, ".svg"), width = w, height = h)
  print(plot)
  dev.off()

  # Vector PDF with embedded fonts
  grDevices::cairo_pdf(paste0(filename, ".pdf"), width = w, height = h, family = "sans")
  print(plot)
  dev.off()

  # High-DPI TIFF for publication print
  ragg::agg_tiff(paste0(filename, ".tiff"), width = w, height = h, units = "in", res = dpi)
  print(plot)
  dev.off()

  # PNG for rapid preview
  ggsave(paste0(filename, ".png"), plot, width = w, height = h, dpi = 150)
}

save_pub_r(p, "plots/Supplementary_Figure_10", width_mm = 150, height_mm = 80)
```
